_comment: Round-16: findings from an external multi-model panel (codex gpt-5.6-sol at xhigh, kimi k3-256k at max thinking, antigravity on gemini-3.1-pro-high), each running the SAME full end-to-end brief rather than a divided one. Two classes, both the same root shape the earlier rounds kept producing — the classifier assuming a POSITION instead of proving a fact. (1) FLAG-BEFORE-VERB: `sf -o my-org data delete bulk ...` is ordinary oclif syntax, but subcommand() stops at the first non-global flag and the fallback re-scan then treats the flag's VALUE as the first positional, giving ('my-org','data','delete') — matching no rule, so bulk delete, anonymous Apex and WHERE-less update were all classified None and allowed with no token and no shield. The verb is now found by anchoring on the sf TOPIC wherever the flags sit. (2) SED W / LINE EDITORS: sed's `w FILE`, `W FILE` and `s///w FILE` commands write a file with no -i flag, so the in-place check never saw them and sed counted as a pure reader; ed and ex write their operand outright. Reaching a gate file that way only fails closed, but the same vectors reach local/writable-orgs.json, and adding a production org to the write allowlist is an escalation rather than a denial of service.
